_readme: Edit this file to add your Amazon affiliate links — nothing else needs touching.
Put your Associates tag in affiliate_tag and it is appended to every amazon.* URL
that does not already carry a tag. Leave a url empty and the card shows a
'link coming soon' button instead of a dead link.
Prices are plain text: keep them vague ('about $45') so they do not go stale.

kits.title: The recommended kit
kits.blurb: What most people should buy. A Pi 4 with 2 GB is overkill for DNS, which is exactly why it will still be fine in five years.

kits.title: The cheap kit
kits.blurb: A Pi Zero 2 W handles a busy family home without breaking a sweat. Slower blocklist updates, same blocking.

kits.title: Other Pi boards
kits.blurb: Pi 3 and Pi 5 boards both work too. Use this tab if you already know which board you want, then add the same card and cable basics plus a matching power supply.

kits.title: The no-thinking kit
kits.blurb: One box with everything in it. Costs a little more than buying the parts separately; saves you three deliveries.

products.name: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B (2 GB)
products.why: The brain. 2 GB is plenty — this software uses well under 100 MB. Any Pi 3, 4 or 5 works too.
products.watch: Buy the board on its own only if you already have a USB-C supply and a card.

products.name: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W
products.why: Cheapest board that is comfortably fast enough. Wi-Fi built in; add the USB adapter below if you want wired.
products.watch: Needs a micro-USB power supply and a mini-HDMI cable if you ever want a screen.

products.name: Raspberry Pi 3 Model B / 3B+
products.why: Still fast enough for adblockerpro and a good choice if you find one cheaply or already have one.
products.watch: Uses micro-USB power, not USB-C. Make sure the supply can deliver a steady 5 V at 2.5 A.

products.name: Raspberry Pi 5
products.why: Works perfectly and has far more performance than DNS filtering needs. Buy it if you want the newest board or will reuse it later.
products.watch: Needs a Pi 5-compatible case and a strong USB-C power supply. Extra RAM does not help adblockerpro.

products.name: 32 GB A2 microSD card (SanDisk / Samsung)
products.why: Where the operating system lives. A2-rated cards survive years of small writes; bargain-bin cards do not.
products.watch: Bigger is not better here. 32 GB is the sweet spot.

products.name: Official Raspberry Pi USB-C power supply (5 V 3 A)
products.why: The single most common cause of a Pi 'randomly' misbehaving is a phone charger that cannot hold 5 V.
products.watch: Must be 3 A. A 2.4 A charger will brown-out under load.

products.name: Micro-USB power supply (5 V 2.5 A)
products.why: For the Pi Zero 2 W. Same rule: a real supply, not a spare phone charger.
products.watch: Micro-USB, not USB-C — the Zero uses the older plug.

products.name: Aluminium passive-cooling case for Pi 4
products.why: It runs 24/7 in a cupboard. A metal case keeps it cool with no fan noise.
products.watch: Make sure the case matches your exact board model.

products.name: Official Raspberry Pi Zero case
products.why: Keeps dust and curious fingers off the board.

products.name: Cat-8 ethernet patch cable (short)
products.why: Plug the Pi into the router. Wired means the filter never drops out when the Wi-Fi hiccups.
products.watch: Short is fine — it is sitting next to the router. Cat-6 or better is plenty; Cat-8 is fine too.

products.name: USB-OTG to ethernet adapter
products.why: Optional for the Pi Zero 2 W if you would rather not rely on Wi-Fi.
products.watch: Needs a micro-USB OTG plug, not the normal USB-A kind.

products.name: Raspberry Pi 4 starter kit (board, case, PSU, card)
products.why: Everything in one box, usually with the card already flashed with Raspberry Pi OS.
products.watch: Check it includes a 5 V 3 A supply and at least a 32 GB card.

products.name: USB microSD card reader
products.why: Only if your laptop has no card slot — you need one to write the operating system.
